findings.summary: The trigger vocabulary comes from the three cited jobs, not from the class. Common inflections and common speed wording are not triggers, so the class is only partly prevented.
findings.evidence: `has_phrase` (surveys.rs:39-45) matches whole words only. With the planned tables, `delayed`, `delays`, `speeds up`, `sped up`, `slows`, `slowdown`, `shortens` and `takes longer` never trigger. For example, `the PR is delayed by 12 minutes` is a delay claim with a figure, and nothing catches it. Verbs such as `reduce`, `cut` and `save` are absent, so `Reduce the CI wait from 10 minutes` is not caught. The plan itself keeps `ci-wait-time-spent-reading` (`Reduce time spent waiting for CI`, refusal_corpus.rs:482-490) as an Accept case that 'names no claim', but that is a speed request. The same goes for `Raise the throughput of the drain queue` (refusal_corpus.rs:473-481). The steward's own slowdown request (hestia.rs:2398-2413: `takes longer`, `shortens that stage`) would also not trigger. The request asks that 'the whole class is prevented', and criterion 3 says 'for the cause and not only for one job'. Fix: Build the trigger from the class. List inflected forms explicitly, as `requires_existing_code_section` does with REUSE (surveys.rs:1360-1369): delay/delays/delayed, speed up/speeds up/sped up, slow/slows/slowdown, takes longer. Add reduce/cut/save/shave combined with a time word (time, wait, minutes, duration) or a figure. Decide each existing Accept case on purpose. Either turn `ci-wait-time-spent-reading` into a Refuse case for this check, or state why a speed request without a figure or stage noun is exempt. Add corpus cases for `delayed` + figure and `speeds up the tests`. Step 8 says 'fix the trigger tables, not the fixture'; reconcile it with any fixture that is truly a speed request.
findings.location: Plan Decision 2 and Step 2 (the speed/delay phrase tables); surveys.rs:39-45 (has_phrase)

findings.summary: `shorten` plus a common stage noun (`tests`, `checks`, `build`, `ci`) will refuse readings about text length.
findings.evidence: In this repository `shorten` usually refers to text, not time: HISTORY.txt:737 `shorten status() under limits`, reading/retry.rs:686, slots.rs:155. Prompt-budget work is common (system facts: reader 1998 of 2000), and a request such as `Shorten the reader prompt so the budget tests pass` would trigger the stage-noun branch. Root-cause requests also quote introspection text verbatim, so a speed phrase and the word `tests` can appear in a request whose fix is unrelated. Fix: Drop `shorten`, or count it only with a time object (time, wait, stage duration). Add an Accept corpus case for a prompt-shortening request that mentions tests.
findings.location: Plan Decision 2 (strong speed phrases and stage nouns)

findings.summary: The `newly refused` exemption is wider than the sibling check it claims to mirror.
findings.evidence: `records_measure_trigger` (surveys.rs:452-460) only skips the declaring criterion; the summary and the other criteria are still searched. The plan instead exempts the whole reading, request and summary included. Any reading that carries a refusal-share declaration therefore skips the check, even when it truly changes pipeline speed. Fix: Either say that the exemption is wider and give the reason, or narrow it. For example, skip only the declaring criterion plus the quoted introspection/prevention block of a root-cause request (the lines after `The introspections that record it:`), and keep scanning the rest.
findings.location: Plan Decision 1 and Step 2 (`timing_claim_trigger` returns None when a criterion contains `newly refused`)

findings.summary: The example Timeline path `crates/athena-core/src/run.rs` does not exist.
findings.evidence: There is no `crates/athena-core/src/run.rs`; `run` is a module directory (`run/mod.rs`, `run/planning.rs`, and so on). The unit tests pass `repo_files` None, so this never shows in them. In production, `check_reading_references` (checks.rs:408-473) refuses any path that is not in the snapshot. If the error example names that path and the reader copies it, the second read is refused by another check. Fix: Use existing paths in the fixture and in the error example, such as `crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs`. Add an assertion that the example in the error text also passes `check_reading_references` with the snapshot's real file set.
findings.location: Plan Demonstration criterion 3, step 2, and the error-text example in Step 3

findings.summary: `estimate` satisfies the source label, and the reader has no records to measure from. A reader can restate the request's own figure as an estimate and pass.
findings.evidence: System facts: readers get a plain copy without `records/`. The three introspections asked for durations measured from a real run. The accepted reading allows estimates, so this is not a misreading of the request, but the refusal text could point the reader to a real source. Fix: In the error text, name where measured stage durations live (the stage medians that `athena status` prints, from Hestia's StageMinutes). Ask the reader to state whether the request's own figure matches the timeline, or else label the figure an unchecked estimate.

findings.summary: The INPUT_FORMS length arithmetic is wrong.
findings.evidence: refusal_corpus.rs:90 already declares `const INPUT_FORMS: [&str; 63]`. The plan adds five new tags (timing-claim-stage-noun, timeline-assumption-satisfied, timeline-missing-parts, docs-class-speed-claim, refusal-declaration-exempt), so the new length is 68. Fix: Set the array length to 63 plus the number of new tags actually added.
findings.location: Plan Decision 5 ('63 becomes the new length') and Step 6

findings.evidence: `replay_declaration(criteria: &[Criterion], out_of_scope)` (replay.rs:263) reads criterion texts. The existing test wraps a sentence in a `Criterion` (refusal_corpus.rs:3140-3147). Fix: Wrap the declaration sentence in a Criterion, as the existing test does, and check it separately from the doc-comment text assertions.

summary: I checked the plan's references by reading the snapshot. The anchors it names exist where it says: `refusing_check` and its `step!` list (checks.rs:520-551, `check_records_measure` at 541), `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion` (surveys.rs:237), `records_measure_trigger` (surveys.rs:452), `refuser_for`, `code_reading`, `SURVEY` and `MODIFY_READING` (reading.rs:7049-7081, 7300), and the order tests at reading.rs:8234 and 8714, which pin only the predecessor of each check. D189 is the last decision. The fake reader's reading has content criteria only (fake.rs:312). No test pins what follows `check_records_measure`. The dependents list matches the callers I found by grep (steward.rs:424, main.rs:709, replay, run/tests.rs, drain.rs). Wiring, the corpus cases and the exit table are sound, and every demonstration names a real seam and would fail without the `step!` line. The verdict is revise because of one major soundness finding. The trigger words come from the three cited jobs rather than from the class: whole-word matching misses `delayed`, `speeds up`, `slowdown` and `takes longer`, and verbs like `reduce`, `cut` and `save` are absent. The plan even keeps `Reduce time spent waiting for CI` as an Accept case 'with no claim', so the request's demand that the whole class be prevented is only partly met. The minor findings are false positives from `shorten` with common stage nouns, a `newly refused` exemption wider than the sibling check it claims to mirror, a non-existent example path (`crates/athena-core/src/run.rs`), estimates satisfying the Timeline, and wrong INPUT_FORMS length arithmetic.
